newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson signs $80 mln China contracts.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson signs $80 mln China contracts.

text.p: Swedish telecoms group Ericsson said on Thursday that it had signed two contracts in China worth more than $80 million.
The contracts were with the Jiangsu Post & Telecommunications Administration and were for the expansion of the GSM and TACS mobile networks in Jiangsu province.
The first contract, valued at $60 million, is the second phase expansion of the Jiangsu GSM network, Ericsson said in a statement.
"With this expansion the total capacity of the network will reach nearly one million subscribers," Ericsson said.
The first phase of the contract was signed last year.
The TACS contract, with a value of about $20 million, is the third phase expansion which will increase the TACS network capacity to 300,000 subscribers.
This contract was signed by JPTA and Ericsson's joint venture, Nanjing Ericsson Communication Company Ltd.
The orders include AXE switching and radio base equipment and associated services.
Ericsson said the expansion will be completed and put into service before the end of 1997.
